title: Banter schemas
description: Banter's configuration contracts, in one file. Each top-level entry under $defs that names a file or an API response is a contract something validates against; the rest are shared building blocks. Extend this file rather than adding siblings — one place, so a type cannot be defined twice and drift. Currently covers the model roster (design record: docs/reference/design/model-roster.md). Still to be added: the service registry, and the control plane's config.

nodeRoster.title: Node roster
nodeRoster.description: The roster section of a node's registry.json: the models, the providers that serve them, and the voices those models render. A node declares only what it can verify, and the control plane assembles every node's roster.

ttsModels.description: Synthesis models on this node, each declared once however many providers serve it.

sttModels.description: Speech-to-text models on this node, each declared once however many providers serve it.

providers.description: Keyed by registry service id; a key naming no registered service is a load error. Host, port and name come from that service entry. A service absent from this map is one the platform will not route to.

voices.description: The curated voices: a voice absent from this list does not exist to the platform.

assembledRoster.title: Assembled roster
assembledRoster.description: What the assembler holds: the node rosters side by side, as declared. Each provider is tagged with its host and whether that host is answering; an unreachable node keeps its last known roster, flagged, because a node being down is not evidence its models ceased to exist. A model or voice id declared on two nodes is left out everywhere and named in `collisions`. Recordings and preset keys stay on the node that declares them.

assembledVoice.description: A voice as the assembler serves it: her name and the models that produce her, without recordings or preset keys.

rosterCollision.description: A model or voice id declared on more than one node, and so left out of the assembly.

servedModel.title: Served model
servedModel.description: One entry in the listing a platform-built model server returns. Everything the roster declares about the model comes back, plus what only the server can know: a client asking what a server serves gets the whole answer, not a record it must complete from elsewhere. The runtime key is the exception — it is the server's own handle, and publishing it would invite a caller to send it in place of the platform id.

created.description: Seconds since the epoch. These models are not created by the server, so it reports process start rather than fabricating a per-request timestamp.

loaded.description: Whether this model is resident. For a model capable of both modes, `modes` says which are up.

loadable.description: Whether this model can be made resident over /v1/models/load.

kind.description: What the model is. Reported separately from transport, although the two correlate today: one says what the model is, the other how it is reached, and the API should not assert a coupling it does not guarantee.

transport.description: How the model is reached. A set, not one value: a model capable of both modes is served over the transcription endpoint and the socket, and collapsing that to one would assert a coupling the server does not guarantee. Reported separately from kind — one says what the model is, the other how it is reached.

present.description: Whether the weights are on disk. NOT availability — availability is a platform fact: is there a registered service, does the roster list this model, can the assembler reach the node. This is one input a server contributes, and it is what makes advertising a model whose weights were never downloaded impossible to restate.

modes.description: Which modes are currently resident. Present for a model reporting kind `both`; a caller loads a mode explicitly, and more than one can be resident at once.

name.description: What to call this model in a listing. Carried from the roster: a client asking what a server serves should not have to complete the answer from somewhere else.

params.description: What a load accepts, as the roster declares it. Reported so a caller can discover the choice rather than learn it from a refusal.

variants.description: The model's variants and the parameter values that select each, as the roster declares them.

variant.description: Which variant is resident, for the loaded model that has several.

cloning.description: The model's cloning terms, as declared, with `available` always true: the entry is present only for a model that can clone.

chunkProfile.description: The model's own chunker constraint, reported because a caller sending more text than the model tolerates gets degraded audio and no error.

presetVoices.description: The voices with a preset rendering on this model, derived from the roster's voices; each id is the voice's id.

canClone.description: Whether this model can render a voice from a reference recording. The common half of `cloning`, which states the whole rule.

requiresRefText.description: Whether cloning under this model needs a transcript alongside the audio.

provider.description: A registered service that serves models. A serving names a model of the provider's capability, checked at load.

resolvesVoices.description: Whether this runtime resolves voices itself by reading the registry; otherwise the shard resolves for it. Required on a synthesis provider.

responseFormat.description: The audio format this runtime returns from /v1/audio/speech, the same for every model it serves. Absent means mp3.

sessions.description: Whether this runtime's streaming socket understands session ids and take-over. Absent means no.

defaultModel.description: The STT model a request naming none loads into an empty slot. Must name a served model that needs no parameter.

idleUnloadMs.description: How long an STT runtime's model may go without work before it is unloaded. Absent or not positive means 30 minutes.

assembledProvider.description: A provider as the assembler serves it: its node's host and reachability, its name from the service entry, and what it serves.

reachable.description: Whether the provider's host is answering; false means this is its last known roster.

name.description: From the service entry, falling back to the service id.

responseFormat.description: The audio format this runtime returns from /v1/audio/speech. mp3 where the roster declares none.

resolvesVoices.description: Whether this runtime resolves voices itself rather than having the shard do it.

sessions.description: Whether this runtime's streaming socket understands session ids and take-over. Absent means no.

serves.description: The models this runtime runs, less any left out as collisions.

sttModel.description: An ASR model: an identity, what it is capable of, and what it accepts. It names no Swift class, loader or directory.

id.description: The platform's identity for this model, used by selections and by anything referring to it.

kind.description: What the model can do. A model reporting `both` must be asked to load with an explicit mode.

params.description: What a load of this model accepts, each with the values it may take. A parameter selects weights only where a variant maps it.

variants.description: The distinct sets of weights under this id. Absent, the model has one implicit variant. Each names the parameter values that select it.

params.description: The parameter values that select this variant. No two variants of a model may be selected by the same values.

ttsModel.description: A synthesis model: this set of weights, whichever runtime serves it.

id.description: The platform's identity for this model, used by selections and renderings.

chunkProfile.description: The model's own chunker constraint for the generation pipeline, not a preference.

chunking.description: How the realtime voice loop splits text for this model.

cloning.description: What this model demands of a recording; whether a recording satisfies it is computed at load. Absent means the model cannot clone.

requiresText.description: The model is sent the transcript alongside the audio.

sampleRate.description: Required rate, where the model constrains it.

voice.description: A person with a name, independent of any model. A voice is offered on a model when she has a rendering on it.

recordings.description: Audio of this voice that models clone her from. Declared order is the preference.

renderings.description: The models that produce this voice, and how. Declared order is the preference.

loadRequest.description: What POST /v1/models/load accepts. A model that offers a choice must be told which: loading a both-capable model with no mode, or a model with chunk sizes with no chunkMs, is refused naming the model and its choices, rather than defaulted into a latency the caller did not pick.

model.description: A model id as listed by /v1/models.

mode.description: Required when the model reports kind `both`; rejected when it reports one kind that this does not name. `both` makes all components resident.

variant.description: Which of the model's variants to load, by id. Refused when given with parameters that select a different variant.

chunkMs.description: The chunkMs parameter, for a model declaring it; must be one of its values. Where a variant maps the value, it selects that variant. A model with several variants must be given a variant or parameters that select one.

sttSelection.description: Which transcription a voice session asks for. A selection, not a definition: every field here names something the roster declares, and none of it says what exists. Tuning that belongs to this use rather than to the model — how long a pause ends a turn, what counts as noise — lives here too, because the same model serves differently in different places.

serviceId.description: The registered service to transcribe through. Names a provider in the assembled roster.

model.description: A model id the chosen provider serves. The server starts holding nothing and never loads implicitly, so a session loads this before its first utterance; without it nothing can be transcribed.

preferStreaming.description: Which half of a model reporting kind `both` to load. Consulted only there — a model that does one thing is not a choice, and this cannot make a batch model stream. Absent, batch: the more accurate of the two, and what the loop did before streaming existed.

chunkMs.description: Which streaming latency tier to load, for a model declaring the chunkMs parameter; must be one of its values. Where the roster maps the value to a variant, this selects it.

reconnect.description: What a voice session does when its streaming socket drops. It reconnects rather than ending voice; words the dropped socket held unfinalized are lost. The first attempt goes at once and each one after waits delayMs longer than the last. A socket that stays up for stableMs resets the count.

attempts.description: Failed connections in a row after which voice ends. Zero ends voice on the first drop.

delayMs.description: How much longer each attempt after the first waits than the one before it.

stableMs.description: How long a socket must stay up before its drop starts a fresh count. One that drops sooner counts as a failure, so a fault that recurs just after the server accepts the session still ends voice.

maxRecordingMs.description: How long an utterance may run before it is flushed regardless of turn detection. A safety net against a wedged VAD sitting on audio indefinitely, not a turn-taking setting.

settleOnStopMs.description: How long voice-off waits for an utterance still being heard or held paused to finish transcribing before closing the transport regardless.

pauseFlushMs.description: How long a paused utterance keeps streaming silence in the microphone's place, so a streaming model transcribes the words it already holds; it produces text for buffered audio only as further audio arrives behind it.

reveal.description: Pacing bounds for the streaming partial's word-by-word reveal.

minIntervalMs.description: Fastest interval between revealed words, in ms. Default: 55.

maxIntervalMs.description: Slowest interval between revealed words, in ms. Default: 200.

vad.description: What counts as speech rather than noise. Applied after a turn ends, to decide whether it is worth transcribing at all.

minSpeechDurationS.description: Utterances shorter than this are discarded.

minSpeechProb.description: Peak speech probability an utterance must reach to be kept.

turnTaking.description: When a turn is over. A pause is detected, smart-turn judges whether the speaker is finished or mid-thought, and the commit is delayed accordingly — longer where the verdict is that more is coming.

pauseThresholdMs.description: Silence after speech before the pause is considered one worth judging.

commitMinDelayMs.description: The wait after a pause smart-turn is confident ended a turn.

commitMaxDelayMs.description: The wait after a pause smart-turn reads as mid-thought. The speaker resuming cancels the commit, which is what this time is for.

smartTurnThreshold.description: At or above this probability the turn is taken as ended, earning the minimum delay.

smartTurnLowCutoff.description: Below this the turn is taken as unfinished, earning the maximum delay. Between the two the delay is interpolated along the curve.

curve.description: How a probability between the cutoffs maps onto a delay.

interruptionMinRemainingS.description: Seconds of speech still to play for a barge-in to count as interrupting something, rather than landing on audio that was ending anyway.

serving.description: One model run by one runtime, with the facts true of this runtime rather than of the weights.

model.description: The id of a declared model of this provider's capability.

key.description: What this runtime calls the model; the same model has a different key under a different runtime.

streaming.description: The runtime can stream this model's audio as it renders. Absent means no.

realtime.description: Fast enough for the realtime voice loop. Absent means no.

concurrency.description: Most requests the realtime voice loop sends this model at once.

requestParams.description: Fields passed verbatim into every synthesis request for this model, in this runtime's vocabulary.

rendering.description: A voice as produced by one model. A preset carries the model's own key for her; a clone carries none.

model.description: The id of a declared synthesis model.

method.description: `preset`: the model was trained with her. `clone`: the model imitates her from one of her recordings.

key.description: The model's own name for the voice. Required for a preset, absent for a clone.

recording.description: Facts about a recording, declared rather than probed from the file.

audio.description: Absolute path to the audio, on the node that declares it.
